issues.display_title: Issue #4359: fix(nadir): resolve useNavigate is not defined crash in Upload modal
issues.main_description_html:
Description

Clicking the "Upload Nadir" button on /my-tours/:mid/nadir causes an unhandled runtime error:
ReferenceError: useNavigate is not defined.

Root Cause

In src/pages/Tour/Detail/Nadir/Components/Upload.jsx, during a previous refactor converting navigation buttons into semantic links, useNavigate was removed from the imports. However, an unused hook declaration const navigate = useNavigate(); remained in the component body. When the Upload modal rendered, executing this line triggered a runtime exception.

A similar unused const navigate = useNavigate(); declaration was also cleaned up from src/pages/Tour/Detail/Publish/Publish.jsx.

Solution

  • Removed the obsolete const navigate = useNavigate(); from Upload.jsx.
  • Cleaned up unused useNavigate import and hook declaration in Publish.jsx.
  • Audited all 809 frontend source files for unbound identifiers and syntax errors.

Result

Screencast.From.2026-10-07.09-23-10.mp4
  • Commit: afc9bc962 (pushed to development)
  • Verification Evidence:
    • Full codebase AST scan: 0 unbound calls or missing hook declarations across 809 files.
    • Production build: Compiled successfully with post-build-filter.js clean exit.
    • Jest test suite: 92/93 test suites passed (631/632 tests passed; 1 unrelated legacy mock test failure in crm.test.js).

issues.display_title: Issue #4357: Refine telemetry sub-labels on Support Analytics KPI cards
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

Refine telemetry sub-labels on the KPI overview cards on /support/analytics to clearly distinguish between core Countly session metrics and actual custom events.

Problem Statement

The KPI cards previously showed event: user_session and event: session_started. These were technically misleading because user_session and session_started are not custom Countly events, but internal aliases for Countly's built-in session metrics (u and t).
Real custom events (registration_completed, payment_completed, tour_created) should retain their event key, while core session metrics should be properly labeled.

Scope of Changes

  • In src/pages/Support/Analytics/Analytics.jsx:
    • Active Users: metric: distinct users
    • User Sessions: metric: total sessions
    • Retain event: <key> on actual custom events: registration_completed, payment_completed, tour_created.
    • Update unit tests (Analytics.test.jsx).

Acceptance Criteria

  • Active Users displays metric: distinct users.
  • User Sessions displays metric: total sessions.
  • Event-based cards display their real event keys (event: ...).
  • All unit tests pass cleanly.

Result

  • Pull Request: #4358 (targets development)
  • Key Commit: cb7240267 — fix(support): use metric label for session telemetry and keep event keys for custom events (#4357)
  • Verification Evidence:
    • Ran Jest unit tests: npm test -- --watchAll=false src/pages/Support/Analytics/Analytics.test.jsx
    • Output: 6 passed, 6 total (100% pass rate).

issues.display_title: Issue #4360: Display local time details in Support Analytics date range banner
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

Enhance the date range banner on /support/analytics to display timestamps formatted in the user's local timezone (e.g., 2026-09-08 07:00 to 2026-10-07 10:15 (WIB)), reflecting real-time data up to the last fetch timestamp.

Problem Statement

Currently, the telemetry banner displays raw date strings without time (Range: 2026-09-08 to 2026-10-07).
Because Countly tracks metrics in near real-time and dates in the API represent UTC boundaries:

  • Support agents cannot easily see whether "today's" data covers the entire day or is a live cut-off up to the current moment.
  • Support agents cannot easily correlate UTC boundaries with their actual working business hours in local time.

Scope of Changes

  • In src/pages/Support/Analytics/Analytics.jsx:
    • Format start_date (00:00:00 UTC) into local browser datetime (YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm).
    • Format end_date:
      • If end_date is today, format up to the live fetched_at timestamp.
      • If end_date is a past date, format up to end of day (23:59:59 UTC).
    • Include the local timezone code/offset (e.g. (WIB) / (GMT+7)).
    • Gracefully fallback to plain dates if timestamps are unavailable.
  • In src/pages/Support/Analytics/Analytics.test.jsx:
    • Add test cases verifying local datetime range rendering.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Range displays full date and time in the user's local browser timezone.
  • For current day ranges, the end time reflects the real-time fetched_at cut-off.
  • Local timezone is indicated alongside the range.
  • All unit tests pass with 100% assertions.

Result

  • Pull Request: #4361 (targets development)
  • Key Commit: a616339ec — feat(analytics): display local time details in support analytics date range banner (#4360)
  • Verification Evidence:
    • Unit test suite: npm test -- --watchAll=false src/pages/Support/Analytics/Analytics.test.jsx -> 9/9 tests passed (100% pass rate).
    • ESLint: 0 errors and 0 warnings.
    • Production build: npm run build compiled successfully and post-build decrypt filter exited cleanly.

issues.display_title: Issue #4351: [Feature] Countly Analytics Tracking for Global Action Receiver (RAG Copilot)
issues.main_description_html:
Overview

Integrate Countly analytics tracking for the Global Action Receiver components in GoThru Dashboard (Layout.jsx and Level.jsx) that handle interactive RAG Copilot client signals (gothru:action).

This complements the widget-side tracking implemented in GoThruMedia/frontend-rag-system#60 by instrumenting the host dashboard execution phase. It isolates and categorizes all RAG action execution metrics using the standard rag_* namespace and segmentation metadata (feature: 'rag_copilot', source: 'dashboard_host') so that the complete conversion funnel from action offer -> trigger -> host execution can be analyzed in Countly without polluting core dashboard metrics.

Tracking Design & Event Schema

1. Event Namespace & Segmentation

All events must follow the rag_ prefix and include standardized categorization:

Event Name Trigger Condition Segmentation Properties
rag_client_action_executed Dashboard successfully executes a received gothru:action event (modal open, route navigation, file picker trigger) feature: "rag_copilot", source: "dashboard_host", action: string, target: string, status: "success"
rag_client_action_failed Dashboard fails to execute the action (e.g. target DOM element missing, invalid/unsupported action) feature: "rag_copilot", source: "dashboard_host", action: string, target: string, status: "failed", reason_code: string

2. Privacy & Safety Boundaries

  • Allowed: feature, source, action, target, status, reason_code.
  • Disallowed: No user tokens, auth headers, search queries, prompt texts, tour IDs / mid in raw strings (normalize route paths to patterns like /my-tours/:mid/upload), or arbitrary payload params.

Technical Approach & Implementation Scope

  1. Countly Schema Sanitization (src/utils/countly.js):

    • Expand ENUM_VALUES or schema whitelist to support RAG event metadata:
      • feature: ['rag_copilot']
      • source: add 'dashboard_host' and 'rag_widget'
      • action: add RAG actions ['open_modal', 'navigate', 'trigger_file_picker']
      • target: validate safe target keys (create_tour_menu, create_hosted_tour, create_google_business, add_level_modal, browse_files, /storage, /my-tours, /my-tours/:mid/upload, etc.)
      • status: ['success', 'failed']
      • reason_code: ['element_not_found', 'unsupported_action']
    • Ensure countlyEvent properly records rag_* events without dropping properties during sanitization.

  2. Global Action Component Instrumentation:

    • src/components/layouts/Layout.jsx:
      • In handleGlobalAction, record rag_client_action_executed when:
        • action === 'open_modal' opens the requested modal (create_tour_menu, create_hosted_tour, create_google_business).
        • action === 'navigate' navigates to the target route (with path normalized via normalizeCountlyPath).
        • action === 'trigger_file_picker' successfully triggers the file input or drag area click.
      • Record rag_client_action_failed if file picker element / drag area cannot be located in DOM or action is unhandled.
    • src/pages/Tour/Components/Level.jsx:
      • In handleAddLevelAction, record rag_client_action_executed with action: 'open_modal', target: 'add_level_modal'.

  3. Verification & Testing:

    • Update src/utils/countly.test.js to ensure the new schema and events pass sanitization without warnings or stripped keys.
    • Add/update unit tests in src/components/layouts/Layout.test.jsx (or Layout.countly.test.jsx) and src/pages/Tour/Components/Level.test.jsx.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Countly utility (src/utils/countly.js) validates and passes rag_client_action_executed and rag_client_action_failed with all allowed segmentations.
  • Executing open_modal, navigate, and trigger_file_picker in Layout.jsx records rag_client_action_executed with status: 'success'.
  • Opening add_level_modal via handleAddLevelAction in Level.jsx records rag_client_action_executed.
  • Action execution failure or missing target elements emit rag_client_action_failed with appropriate reason_code.
  • Route paths in target are normalized to avoid leaking specific tour IDs or query strings.
  • Zero PII or arbitrary payload objects are forwarded to Countly.
  • 100% unit test coverage for new/modified action handlers and Countly utils.

Part of Epic: GoThruMedia/gothru-rag#29
Related to: GoThruMedia/frontend-rag-system#60, #4343
